about: Every fact, step and limit this update says or shows, with the source's own words. Sources: three OpenAI pages and Todd's own ChatGPT Business Hub screens, all read and captured on Nov 12, 2026 (Central) in the browser on his PC during the live chat he started for this lesson (2:46 pm). OpenAI's pages answer our page reader and WebFetch with a 403, so each was read in full as text in his browser and the passages used were captured there; the captures in 04_scene/assets/ are the record a reviewer checks. The lesson has one number: OpenAI's own 1.2 billion weekly users. It names no person and no business but OpenAI, ChatGPT, Persona, Shopify, Google (the send line) and ProofNotFluff (ours). Not said, though the pages say it: Business Agents, product feeds, insights, the blue check, the claim invitation and locked listing cases, dispute of ownership, what can be edited after approval (website, description, category, logo, policies). Not claimed: that Business Hub is missing from anyone else's sidebar (one account was seen); that trades businesses are or are not 'local stores' (the help page's own words, 'local stores and restaurants', are used; the voice asks 'A plumber or a roofer? Search and see.' and states nothing about trades); anything about ranking beyond OpenAI's own 'doesn't guarantee'. Round 1 (after the viewer and render critic failed render 2): the 'we searched ours' story, the DNS record, Persona's name, the email decision and the sidebar screen are no longer said or shown; nothing was added but OpenAI's weekly user figure and the line 'A plumber or a roofer? Search and see.', which claims nothing.

claims.words: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT; dated November 10, 2026

claims.said: One point two billion people use it every week
claims.words: the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week

claims.said: But read the small print before you claim yours
claims.words: By continuing, you accept OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT Terms.
claims.note: advice, tied to the terms line on his own screen

claims.said: It's called Business Hub, it's in beta, and it's where you claim your business
claims.words: We're introducing Businesses in ChatGPT in beta ... Through Business Hub, businesses can claim their business

claims.said: One. Open Business Hub. OpenAI says it's in your sidebar
claims.words: Sign in to ChatGPT, and open Business Hub from the sidebar.

claims.said: or type chatgpt.com slash business hub
claims.words: the address bar on his own screenshot reads chatgpt.com/business-hub (followed by the create flow's own ?create=1&creation_session=1)
claims.note: on screen the address is written exactly, with its hyphen: chatgpt.com/business-hub. Claude opened the Business Hub page at exactly https://chatgpt.com/business-hub in his signed-in Chrome at 3:06 pm (the browser tool's own log); the capture that shows an address bar is his 3:27 pm screenshot (asset hub-address). On his account the sidebar did not show Business Hub; the video says 'or' and claims nothing about other accounts.

claims.words: Search for your business by name.; the box reads 'Search business'

claims.said: Now the small print. By continuing, you accept OpenAI's terms
claims.words: By continuing, you accept OpenAI's Businesses in ChatGPT Terms.

claims.said: They say its AI assistant may call your business for its users. You can opt out
claims.words: By using Business Hub, you agree OpenAI's AI assistant may make calls to you on behalf of our users. You can opt out here.

claims.said: And you agree not to bring certain claims against OpenAI
claims.words: Covenant Not to Sue. You ... covenant and agree not to assert or commence ... any Covered Claim against OpenAI or any of its Affiliates
claims.note: 'certain claims' stands for the terms' defined 'Covered Claim'; never 'you can't sue OpenAI'

claims.said: Here's the catch. OpenAI says local stores and restaurants can only claim a listing that's already there. U.S. only, for now
claims.words: Local stores and restaurants can currently claim only an existing U.S. listing.
claims.note: 'for now' is the page's 'currently'. The catch is stated only for the page's own group, local stores and restaurants; the voice never says 'local businesses' or 'if you're local' (facts gate, script round after the rewrite)

claims.said: A plumber or a roofer? Search and see
claims.note: claims nothing: the help page's words are 'local stores and restaurants' and the video does not say whether a trade business counts; it tells the viewer to look

claims.said: Three. Prove it's yours with your business phone or email, or your website
claims.words: Use one of the verification methods offered for your business, such as phone, business email, website domain, or Shopify. Heading: Verify with your business phone. His own screenshot: Verify that you control proofnotfluff.com
claims.note: three of the page's examples; Shopify is left out; never 'every business gets all of them'

claims.said: Four. Pass an identity check before any change goes live
claims.words: You'll need to complete identity verification with Persona before you can publish changes to your business information; You may need a government-issued ID
claims.note: Persona is not named in the voice

claims.said: And OpenAI says claiming it doesn't guarantee ChatGPT recommends you more
claims.words: It doesn't guarantee increased visibility or give you direct control over ChatGPT's independent recommendations.

claims.said: Save this, and send it to whoever runs your Google listing
claims.note: the send line; it claims nothing about Google

posts: Queued first for the evening slot on Nov 12, 2026 (8:13 pm Central), two days after the announcement; the slug's date is its place in line, not its post day. If it has not posted by Nov 17, re-read the help page and the terms before it does, and drop 'just'.
weeklyUsersNote: OpenAI's own figure in the announcement: 'the 1.2 billion people who use ChatGPT each week' (asset announce-beta). Said as 'one point two billion people use it every week'.
